summary: Jotunheim Valley is a high, mainly ice-free valley in the Asgard Range of Victoria Land, Antarctica, lying east of Wolak Peak and Utgard Peak, with Saint Pauls Mountain at its head. The New Zealand Antarctic Place-Names Committee named it in 1982 on a proposal from G.G.C. Claridge, a soil scientist with the DSIR, New Zealand. The name comes from Norse mythology, Jotunheim being the home of the giants, and is one of several Norse-derived names in the Asgard Range.
one_line: Jotunheim Valley is an ice-free valley in Antarctica's Asgard Range, named in 1982 after the Norse home of the giants.
